title: fix: restore public GitHub app submission KPIs
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes the optional GitHub token dependency from public app-submission and repository stats; no credentials changed.
- Caches successful public responses for 30 minutes while preserving pagination and explicit upstream failures.
- Adds regression coverage for cached pagination, PR exclusion, week boundaries, and failed-page recovery.
- Verified 43 tests, the Worker route bundle, and live GitHub reads (32 submissions for the September 21 week).
- Production currently returns 502; the exact upstream credential or rate-limit failure remains unconfirmed. This PR is not deployed.

gist.headline: Public stats find their footing
gist.blurb: The KPI Worker can read public GitHub app submissions and repository stats without an optional token. Successful responses get a 30-minute rest; upstream errors still speak for themselves.
gist.summary: The KPI Worker now reads public GitHub app-submission and repository stats without an optional token and caches successful responses for 30 minutes, while preserving pagination and explicit upstream failures.
gist.impact: Once deployed, public KPI views can use token-free GitHub reads for weekly submission totals and repository stats; the production 502 has not yet been verified as resolved.
gist.visual_concept: Polli checks a small ledger of weekly app submissions beside a friendly CRT robot showing paginated GitHub pages. A lime-green garden path connects the pages to a public stats board; a modest clock represents the 30-minute cache. Avoid depicting the production 502 as already fixed.
